Drivers of four-wheeled vehicles and larger vehicles

Drivers may experience drowsiness while driving and display observable signs such as heavy eyelids, frequent yawning, and head nodding. These signs may not always be recognized immediately, which may affect the driver’s attentiveness while operating a vehicle.

Trusted Contacts may need a practical way to remain informed about drowsiness-alert information shared by a Driver, particularly when records cannot be synchronized immediately because internet connectivity is unavailable.

Develop DriveAlert, an IoT-based driver drowsiness monitoring and alert system that monitors prolonged eye closure, yawning, and head nodding, provides warning alerts, stores drowsiness-alert records, and
Provide a Trusted Contact feature in DriveAlert that allows an approved Trusted Contact to review synchronized drowsiness-alert records and related information after the Driver has authorized access.
Drivers experience drowsiness or sleepiness while driving, find warning alerts helpful, and are willing to consider using an affordable and easy-to-use driver-monitoring system.

Potential Trusted Contacts are willing to review Driver-approved alert records, consider the shared information useful, accept delayed synchronization, and are willing to use an easy-to-use Trusted Contact feature.

A survey was conducted among drivers to assess drowsiness or sleepiness while driving, perceived helpfulness of warning alerts, and willingness to use an affordable and easy-to-use monitoring system. Success requires at least 70% positive responses for drowsiness experience and willingness to use the system.

A survey was conducted among potential Trusted Contacts to assess willingness to review shared records, perceived usefulness, acceptance of Driver-approved access and delayed synchronization, and willingness to use the feature. Success requires at least 70% positive acceptance of the Trusted Contact feature.

The survey showed that 95.2% of 42 respondents had experienced drowsiness or sleepiness while driving, while 81.0% were willing to use a system like DriveAlert if affordable and easy to use. Since both exceeded 70%, development will proceed.

The survey showed that 88.2% of 17 respondents were willing to review shared records, 94.1% found the information useful, and 82.4% accepted delayed synchronization and would probably use the feature. Since the results exceeded 70%, the feature will proceed.

The findings showed that drowsiness while driving is relevant among the surveyed drivers and that respondents showed interest in an affordable and easy-to-use monitoring system. These results support further development of DriveAlert’s monitoring and warning functions.

The findings showed that potential Trusted Contacts generally accepted Driver-approved access, delayed synchronization, and shared alert information. These results support retaining and refining DriveAlert’s Trusted Contact and record-sharing functions.

The Driver uses the Android application to connect an authorized DriveAlert device, align the camera, and complete the guided personal calibration while parked. The Driver starts and stops monitoring, previews the camera, receives onboard warnings, and reviews personal alert history, insights, and monitoring logs. The Driver can change warning preferences and manage Trusted Contact requests and approved connections. A primary Driver may also invite additional Drivers through a simulated subscription that collects no real payment. Device registration, invitation acceptance, and initial authorization require internet access. After setup, authorized Drivers can use the device offline while keeping their calibration and alert history separate.

The Trusted Contact uses the Android application or web portal to request and manage approved connections with Drivers. The Trusted Contact reviews eligible shared Stage 3 transition and persistence records, including their warning periods, detected signs, event counts, and synchronization details. The Trusted Contact can accept or decline requests, disconnect from a Driver, and manage shared-history retention and personal record removal. Shared records become available after an eligible upload and provide historical awareness. Trusted Contact access does not include live camera video, vehicle location, complete Driver alert history, or control of the Driver's monitoring session.
